correctness.rationale: For each fixed r, binomial inclusion probabilities give exact covariance q_u-q_a q_b. Nested-set factorization gives nonnegative signs. For incomparable sets, covariance is negative before r=u; after that H_r=q_u/(q_a q_b) has consecutive ratio deviation (ab-c(r+1))/[(r+1)(r+1-u)], giving a single peak. H_n=1 and exact H_{n-1} sign nc-ab yield the full global classification, strict boundaries, and at most one zero at integer stages. This algebra is a proof for every admissible finite n, unlike finite checks. Replayed checker.py: 17,743 exact cardinality/stage checks, 1,650 parameter cases, and 1,737 independently enumerated random-subset comparisons. Scope and limits in RESULT.md.

originality.rationale: A full pairwise coextinction covariance one-switch law was not found in the compared 2004 binary knockout source, the 2010 quantitative/rewiring source, or the 2018 aggregate robustness-distribution source. The classic hypergeometric/negative-association theorem requires disjoint coordinate supports for negative covariance. Exact comparison to an existing rank-covariance result shows distinct random variables and opposite signs on the same n,a,b,c. The verdict is qualified: uninspected generic event-reliability literature may contain an equivalent theorem; negative search is not a novelty certificate.
residual_risks: An algebraically equivalent condition may be stated in older generic reliability, urn-model, or set-inclusion association literature outside the inspected sources; independent historical priority remains unverified.
The 1983 negative-association primary article was examined at abstract level only, so whole-document noncoverage is not asserted.
The binary removal rule is an idealized ecological null model and does not establish empirical coextinction predictions.

value.rationale: The covariance of surviving plant indicators supplies the non-marginal contributions to stagewise variance of species richness under a standard ecological knockout null model. The exact threshold c>ab/n is interpretable relative to a random-partner-overlap baseline, and the global one-switch restriction gives a complete natural classification for all cardinalities and finite removal stages, not a free numerical subcase. Its positive-versus-negative reversal is masked by mean robustness curves and cannot be read from integrated extinction-rank covariance alone. The proof deliberately does not imply field realism or a full richness distribution.
